newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rocker denies hoping to be U.S. citizen.
newsitem.headline: French rocker denies hoping to be U.S. citizen.

text.p: Rock star Johnny Hallyday, idolised in France as a Gallic answer to Elvis, sought to reassure distraught fans on Wednesday by denying reports he was planning to seek American citizenship.

"We almost lost Johnny," Le Parisien said, quoting the 53-year-old rocker who has sold some 80 million records as saying: "I'm French and proud of it." The daily France-Soir said in a front-page headline: "American, me? Never!".
Hallyday, with a craggy face and voice to match, was quoted by USA Today on Tuesday as saying he wanted to become an American citizen because "French people are very rude".

The report provoked shock in France where the leather-clad singer is seen as a bulwark against the dominance of English language rock. He was awarded the Legion of d'Honneur, France's highest civilian honour, two weeks ago.

The report quoted Hallyday, who lives much of the year in Florida, as saying he planned to live on a luxury yacht but was looking for a fixed address in the United States to help qualify for citizenship.

He also upset millions in France, whose government is at odds with Washington on issues ranging from NATO to Zaire and which seeks to limit imports of Hollywood movies, by reportedly remarking that: "Everything in America is better".
Ironically, Hallyday is virtually unknown in the United States. The USA Today article called him "the biggest rock star you've never heard of".
"I know that the French people have made me," Hallyday told Le Parisien, saying he had been misquoted in the article. "And by calling them rude, I'd be harming myself."
The daily Liberation quoted him as saying: "If the French are rude, then so am I."

Hallyday has had huge success in a roller-coaster career as a rock star since a first hit in the 1960s when General Charles de Gaulle was president of France. Universally known as "Johnny", he was also a child television star in the mid-1950s.
Hallyday made his American debut last year with a concert in Las Vegas -- but almost all the fans flew from France.
